The Pension Code describes this as a possible duty disability benefit if the injury was incurred in the performance of an act or acts of duty. Otherwise, it may be an ordinary disability benefit if the Code’s ordinary-disability requirements are met. [40 ILCS 5/11-155] [40 ILCS 5/11-156]

For a duty disability benefit, the injury must have occurred after you were included under Article 11 and while you were performing an act or acts of duty. The benefit is payable during the period of disability for which you receive no salary. The Code also says that heart attacks, strokes, and disablement within the broad field of coronary involvement or heart disease are not accidental injuries incurred in the performance of duty. [40 ILCS 5/11-155]

For an ordinary disability benefit, the Code text provided here does not give enough information to decide eligibility. It turns on facts such as when and how the disability began, whether you were absent from duty when it began, whether you have recovered and returned to duty for the required period after a prior disability, and the total period of ordinary disability previously received. [40 ILCS 5/11-156] A duty-disability application also requires a claim with your employer establishing that the disability occurred while you were acting within the scope and course of your duties. [40 ILCS 5/11-158]

The question of whether you can medically perform your job is decided under the Fund’s disability process and medical review, not by the Pension Code text provided here.
